common_name: Hopi Pale Grey Squash (Ancient Southwestern Native American Squash)

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost in warm soil, giving the sprawling vines ample room; this drought-adapted Hopi heirloom tolerates arid conditions better than most winter squash once established.

directions: Direct sow seed an inch deep in hills, giving the vigorous, far-ranging vines generous room to spread. Hopi Pale Grey is a traditional Hopi heirloom squash grown for centuries in the arid Southwest, producing large, round to slightly oval fruit with smooth, pale bluish-gray skin and dense, deep orange, sweet flesh well suited to baking, soups, and traditional Hopi cooking. It is notably drought tolerant once established, reflecting its origins in a low-rainfall growing region, and stores exceptionally well, often keeping through much of the winter in a cool, dry location. Harvest once the rind hardens fully and resists a fingernail scratch, then cure for a couple of weeks in a warm, airy spot before moving to long-term storage.

common_name: Tennessee Sweet Potato Squash (Southern Cushaw-Type Heirloom)

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost in warm, fertile soil, giving vines ample room to run; this Southern heirloom is well adapted to hot, humid summers and performs reliably across the Gulf South.

directions: Direct sow seed an inch deep in hills in full sun, allowing generous room for the sprawling vines. Tennessee Sweet Potato is an old Southern heirloom squash bearing pear- to bell-shaped, buff-tan fruit with a smooth rind and dense, sweet, fine-textured orange flesh reminiscent of sweet potato, a resemblance that gives the variety its name. As a moschata-type squash it shows good resistance to squash vine borer and performs reliably through hot, humid Southern summers, making it a dependable choice for Gulf South gardens where other winter squash struggle. Harvest once the rind hardens and resists a fingernail scratch, then cure for a couple of weeks in a warm, airy spot to concentrate sweetness before moving to cool, dry storage.
